rationale: The available literature establishes that NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A (p.Gly357Arg) is strongly recurrent, accounting for 11 of 14 reported individuals with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, with all variants clustering in the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain. However, the available sources do not provide empirical germline mutation rate quantification or a formal phenotypic severity comparison between the 11 individuals with p.Gly357Arg and the 3 individuals with non-recurrent Kelch-domain variants. Consequently, whether recurrence is driven predominantly by intrinsic CpG hypermutability versus ascertainment bias driven by phenotypic distinctiveness or severity remains unresolved by the provided cohort data.

evidence.text: In a study delineating KLHL20-related neurodevelopmental disorder in 14 individuals with de novo missense variants, 11 harbored the identical recurrent missense variant NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A (p.Gly357Arg), while the remaining 3 harbored distinct missense variants; all clustered in the Kelch-type beta-propeller substrate-binding domain.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, seizures, and behavioral abnormalities
source.quote: We studied 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, delineating a genetic syndrome with patients having mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features. We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]). The recurrent missense and the 3 other missense variants all clustered in the Kelch-type β-propeller domain of the KLHL20 protein

conflicts: No study in the retrieved literature formally compares clinical severity scores (e.g., seizure onset, developmental quotient, structural anomalies) between p.Gly357Arg and non-Gly357Arg Kelch domain variants to rule out differential ascertainment bias.

While c.1069G>A represents a canonical C-to-T transition on the opposite strand at a CpG dinucleotide, intrinsic germline de novo mutation rate models have not been calibrated directly against clinical ascertainment rates for KLHL20.

new_directions.question_text: Does deep sequencing of sperm DNA from healthy control males show an elevated de novo mutation frequency specifically at KLHL20 c.1069G>A compared to other Kelch-domain missense sites?
new_directions.rationale: Direct measurement of ultra-rare de novo transitions in male germline samples would determine the physical mutational rate of c.1069G>A independent of post-zygotic selection or clinical ascertainment bias.

new_directions.question_text: Do functional ubiquitin ligase assays and substrate binding assays reveal distinct biochemical disruption between p.Gly357Arg and other Kelch-propeller variants?
new_directions.rationale: Comparing substrate recruitment kinetics across all known KLHL20 missense alleles would clarify whether p.Gly357Arg confers an identical or uniquely severe biochemical defect.
